01.r: Introduces what the priests are to have.
01.n: The verb is feminine, 'it shall be', and the Hebrew does not say what 'it' is. The Geneva supplies 'the Priesthood'; the DRC and ASV turn the clause into 'they shall have'. Which is meant is uncertain; the following words, 'I am their inheritance', are the clearest answer the verse gives.

02.r: The priests of the restored temple.

03.r: Names what the priests receive as their share.
03.n: Gesenius notes this noun is often used of the territory assigned to each tribe. The DRC reads 'they shall have no inheritance'.

04.r: The LORD names himself as what the priests receive.
04.n: There is no verb in the Hebrew: 'I, their inheritance'. The pronoun is written out, which gives it weight.

05.r: In place of land, the LORD himself is the priests' share.

06.r: Land held as one's own property.
06.n: Gesenius: possession, especially used of the possession of lands and fields. Our register renders this word 'holding', to keep it apart from 'inheritance'; the translations say 'possession'.

07.r: Rules out any grant of land.

08.r: Israel, who will share out the land, must not give the priests any.
08.n: 'You' is plural: the people of Israel addressed as a whole.

10.r: Anywhere in the land of Israel.

11.r: The LORD again names himself as the priests' share.
11.n: Again there is no verb in the Hebrew, and the pronoun is written out.

12.r: The LORD takes the place of the land the priests do not own.
12.n: The same word as 'a holding' earlier in the verse: the holding denied in Israel is answered by the LORD as holding.

_extra.17: ὅτι (for, because): added by the Greek translators; nothing in the Hebrew answers to it.

06.n: κατάσχεσις, a holding, a possession held fast; it comes from κατέχω, hold fast, and so matches our 'holding'.

08.n: δοθήσεται, 'shall be given', a passive where the Hebrew has 'you shall give'.

10.n: ἐν τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἰσραήλ, 'among the sons of Israel'.
